properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From Anthony's VS Code work log (SOURCE: art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05, entry of 2026-10-01, "Hub (multi-design) findings", reflow2 0.76.0), in its words: "'Export once per commit that changed the graph' collides with a store that also holds another session's uncommitted work: committing unrelated changes means either sweeping that WIP into the export or skipping the export. Twice today the export was deferred for this reason. Idea: export a region/epoch range, or `loop_status` listing unexported changes by epoch so the person can choose." Later the same day: "`compare_designs` with `base_path` = the committed export showed exactly which unexported nodes the live store held (49), which is what stopped an export that would have bundled someone's in-progress work."

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE:
- The mechanism is on record: one store serves every branch and session, so an export carries every session's writes (fact:the-live-graph-does-not-branch-so-two-open-prs-collide, first seen 2026-08-14). The served answer for two sessions on one design is `parallel-work`, a worktree with its own copy of the design.
- What is unexported is readable today: `compare_designs` with `base_path` (the reporter's route) and `loop_status` with `since_export`. Neither groups the items by who wrote them or when.
- `export_graph` takes no filter (checked on main, 2026-10-05).
- On main since 2026-10-04 (first released in the next cut), the committed design is one file per node and per edge (dec:how-the-saved-design-is-laid-out-so-git-merges-it). An export rewrites only the files whose item changed, so git can stage a subset of them. The work machine's 0.76.0 still writes the single file.
- Under the accepted blueprint an export is a copy at one moment that reflow2 never tracks (dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy). What goes into a commit is git's question; what reflow2 can supply is which items are whose.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) A SCOPED EXPORT: `export_graph` takes a region (a node set, a claimed region, ids) or an epoch range, and writes only those items.
(b) A SCOPED LIST: `loop_status` (or `compare_designs`) groups the unexported items by epoch, author or seat, so the person picks what to stage. With the item layout that is enough to commit only one's own files.
(c) NOTHING NEW: the item layout plus `compare_designs`, and `parallel-work` when two sessions share a design.

SIZE: (a) moderate to large. A partial export must not write an edge whose endpoint it leaves out, and per-item lineage must still chain. (b) small to moderate, depending on the grouping key: no node records which session wrote it, so "by session" needs the seat or a ChangeEvent. (c) a sentence in a skill.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside it:
- A partial export disagrees with its own store by design. Every later reader (compare_designs, the upstream watch, an import) would have to know it is partial, or it reads the other session's work as deleted.
- In reflow2 an epoch is a planned increment, not a time window. A write is filed under an epoch only when someone draws it, so an epoch range would miss most unexported writes.
- The cause is two sessions sharing one store. Isolating them removes the collision; scoping the export hides it, and the same work in progress meets the next export.
- In favour: the item layout makes (b) cheap to use, because staging a subset of item files is ordinary git.
properties.name: OPEN — when one store holds another session's unexported work, how does a person export only their own: an export of a region or an epoch range, loop_status listing unexported changes by epoch, or nothing new now that the design is saved one file per item?
